title: No recommendations in inquest report after suicide in soon
article: A newly released inquest report has made no recommendations in the case of a man who committed suicide while in custody in a Winnipeg police holding room with no video monitoring.
David Norbert, 56, was found hanging by the neck from a shirt he had tied to a ceiling ventilation grate in a holding room at the District 3 station on Hartford Avenue on April 16, 2019.
The station, the oldest in the city, is considered outdated and is set to be replaced.

Norbert was arrested after allegedly assaulting and threatening an ex-roommate earlier in the day. During an intake interview and risk assessment, Norbert told police he had consumed 11 beers in the previous five hours, the inquest report says. Asked if he was suicidal, Norbert laughed and said, "Sometimes, yes, and sometimes no," before assuring them, "No, of course I'm not."
A toxicology report completed after his death showed Norbert had various drugs in his system, including anti-anxiety medications, that would have impaired his thinking, the inquest report said.

Police officers told the inquest they checked on Norbert at 15-minute intervals, beginning at 8 p.m., until shortly after 10 p.m., when an officer told Norbert he would be taken to the Winnipeg Remand Centre.
"No change was noted in his demeanor, he was still noted to be co-operative," provincial court Judge Murray Thompson wrote in the inquest report.

When an officer checked on Norbert 10 minutes later, he was found hanging from the ceiling grate. Police performed CPR before paramedics arrived. He was taken to Seven Oaks General Hospital and pronounced dead.
The Hartford Avenue station does not have video monitoring in its holding rooms.
"The court was advised that the new building will have facilities like other more modern Winnipeg Police Service buildings, where all the cells are monitored by video," Thompson said.
Since Norbert's death, the ventilation grates in the holding rooms at the station have been replaced with new grates that have much smaller holes, Thompson said.
